primitives.name: RoPE Theta Scaling
primitives.verbatim_quote: The 500k RoPE theta (vs Mistral's 10k, Qwen2.5's 1M) is the long-context knob: Llama's lesson is that **positional-encoding scale is a first-class training decision**, set at pretraining time, and it determines the usable context ceiling more than layer count does.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes fixed pretraining context length; linearly scales with sequence depth; requires walk-forward validation for new domains.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when $\theta$ exceeds model capacity, causing catastrophic forgetting of short-range dependencies.

layer2.mapping: Maps to temporal kernel width $\sigma_t$ in state-space models: $\sigma_t \propto 1/\sqrt{\theta}$.
layer2.telemetry: Measured drop in short-sequence accuracy when extrapolating context length beyond original $\theta$.

primitives.name: KV Cache Optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: Long-context use (128K) multiplies KV-cache memory, so real long-context serving needs GQA's savings (below) plus paged attention.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes constant per-token overhead; neglects sparsity patterns; applies to greedy decoding.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when VRAM < (Batch Size × Context Length × 2 × Param Size in bits / 8).

layer2.mapping: Reduces to query/key projection sparsity in attention matrices: only relevant tokens update.
layer2.telemetry: GPU memory usage spikes quadratically with context length, triggering out-of-memory errors.

primitives.name: Herding Strategy
primitives.verbatim_quote: The "herd" strategy: one architecture family from 8B to 405B so techniques transfer across scales.
primitives.latex: Scale Law: Performance ∝ Model Capacity ^ α
primitives.assumptions: Assumes independent data and parameters; neglects compute bottlenecks; holds for transformer families.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when dataset diversity saturates; additional parameters yield diminishing returns.

layer2.mapping: Maps to curriculum learning in reinforcement: simpler tasks (smaller models) inform policy gradients for larger ones.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-scale performance correlation > 0.95 on held-out benchmarks.

The core challenge is scaling sequence models while preserving computational efficiency and interpretability. Llama-3.1 addresses this via three interdependent mechanisms: (1) RoPE theta controls the effective horizon of temporal dependencies, acting as a learned kernel width; (2) KV-cache reduction via Grouped Query Attention (GQA) mitigates quadratic memory growth, enabling practical 128K contexts; (3) the herding principle ensures architectural consistency across scales, allowing knowledge distillation. These primitives form a dualistic pair: longer contexts require denser representations, but denser representations demand sparser attention. The gated nature of the model introduces a regulatory constraint: performance gains must come from improving the underlying data distribution, not from exploiting architectural loopholes. This leads to a failure mode where aggressive scaling violates the assumed i.i.d. property of training data, causing catastrophic forgetting.
